chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Isa — in a raised chain (mursal).

He said: Verily Musa (peace be upon him) was engaged in intimate discourse (munajaat) with Allah, the Blessed and Exalted. He said to him in His discourse: 'O Musa! Do not let your hope in the world be prolonged, for that would harden your heart, and the hard-hearted one is far from Me. O Musa! Be as My desire of you — My desire is that I be obeyed and not disobeyed. Kill your heart with awe, and wear worn-out clothes with a renewed heart. Be hidden from the people of the earth and be known among the people of the heavens — a permanent dweller in your home, a lamp of the night. Perform qunoot before Me with the qunoot of the patient ones, and cry out to Me from the abundance of sins like the cry of the sinner fleeing from his enemy. Seek help from Me for that, for I am the best Helper and the best One sought for help.

O Musa! Verily I am Allah, above the servants, and the servants are beneath Me, and all are submissive before Me. Accuse your soul regarding your own self, and do not trust your son in your religion unless your son is like you, loving the righteous. O Musa! Wash yourself, perform the ritual bath (ghusl), and draw near to My righteous servants. O Musa! Be their Imam in their prayers and their Imam in what they dispute, and judge between them by what I have revealed to you — for I have sent it down as a clear decree, a luminous proof, and a light speaking of what was among the former ones and what will be among the latter ones.

...and what will be among the latter ones. I bequeath to you, O Musa, the bequest of the compassionate and merciful: regarding the son of the Purified Lady, Isa son of Maryam, owner of the she-donkey, the hooded cloak, the oil, the olive, and the prayer niche. And after him, regarding the owner of the red camel, the pure and purified one. His description in your Book is that he is a believer, guardian over all the Books, bowing, prostrating, desirous and fearful; his brothers are the poor, and his helpers are another people. And in his era there will be hardship, earthquake, killing, and shortage of wealth. His name is Ahmad, Muhammad, the Trustworthy — from the remaining ones, from the group of the first and foremost, who believes in all the Books, affirms all the Messengers, and sincerely bears witness for all the Prophets. His community is shown mercy, blessed, as long as they remain in the religion upon its realities. They have appointed times at which they perform prayers as a servant performs his voluntary devotion for his master. So believe in him and follow his way.

...so follow it, for he is your brother. O Musa! He is unlettered (ummi), and he is a truthful servant. Whatever he places his hand upon is blessed for him, and he is blessed thereby. Such was it in My knowledge, and thus I created him. By him I shall open the Hour, and by his community I shall seal the keys of the world. So command the wrongdoers among the Children of Israel not to erase his name and not to abandon him — though they will surely do so. And loving him is a good deed in My sight; for I am with him, I am of his party, and he is of My party, and their party shall be victorious. My words are fulfilled: I shall surely make his religion prevail over all religions, and I shall be worshipped in every place. And I shall send down upon him a Quran, a Criterion (Furqan), a healing for what is in the chests from the whisperings of Satan. So send blessings upon him, O son of Imran, for I send blessings upon him and so do My angels. O Musa!

O Musa! You are My servant and I am your God. Do not humiliate the despised poor, and do not envy the wealthy for something trivial. Be humble during My remembrance, and yearning for My mercy during its recitation. Let Me hear the sweetness of the Torah with a humble and sorrowful voice. Be tranquil at My remembrance, and remind of Me those who find tranquility in Me. Worship Me and do not associate anything with Me, and seek My pleasure. Verily I am the Great Master. Verily I created you from a drop — from despicable water, from clay which I brought out from lowly, mixed earth. It became a human being and I am its Maker as a creation. Blessed be My Face and sanctified be My handiwork. Nothing is like Me, and I am the Ever-Living, the Eternal who does not perish. O Musa! When you supplicate to Me, be fearful...

...be fearful, apprehensive, and trembling. Press your face in the dust before Me, and prostrate to Me with the noble parts of your body, and perform qunoot before Me in standing. Whisper to Me when you whisper with awe from a trembling heart. Revive My Torah throughout the days of life, and teach My praises to the ignorant, remind them of My favors and My grace, and tell them not to persist in the error they are in, for My seizing is painful and severe. O Musa! If your rope from Me is severed, it will not connect to the rope of another. So worship Me and stand before Me in the station of the humble, poor servant. Condemn your soul, for it is most deserving of condemnation, and do not lord over the Children of Israel with My Book. This is sufficient as an admonition for your heart and an illumination — and it is the speech of the Lord of the Worlds, Exalted and Most High. O

O Musa! Whenever you call upon Me and place hope in Me, I shall surely forgive you for what has come from you. The sky glorifies Me in awe, the angels from fear of Me are apprehensive, the earth glorifies Me eagerly, and all of creation glorifies Me in submission. Then keep to the prayer — the prayer — for it holds a place with Me and has with Me a firm covenant. And join to it what belongs with it: the zakat of the sacrifice from the purest of wealth and food, for I do not accept except the pure that is intended for My sake. And join with that the maintaining of family ties, for I am Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The family bond — I created it preferentially from My mercy so that the servants may show compassion through it, and it holds authority with Me in the return of the Hereafter. I shall cut off the one who severs it and join with the one who maintains it, and that is how I deal with one who neglects My command. O

O Musa! Honor the beggar when he comes to you with a beautiful reply or a small gift, for the one who comes to you may be neither human nor jinn — the angels of the Most Gracious testing you to see how you act with what I have favored you and how you console with what I have granted you. Humble yourself before Me in supplication, and call out to Me with the lament of the Book. Know that I call you as a master calls his slave to elevate him to noble stations, and that is from My favor upon you and upon your early forefathers. O Musa! Do not forget Me in every situation, and do not rejoice at the abundance of wealth, for forgetting Me hardens hearts, and with abundance of wealth comes abundance of sins. The earth is obedient, the sky is obedient, the seas are obedient, and disobedience to Me is the misery of the two weighty ones. I am the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful — Gracious in every era. I bring hardship after ease and ease after hardship, and kings after kings, while My Kingdom is permanent and abiding, never ceasing. Nothing is hidden from Me in the earth or the sky — for how can what originates from Me be hidden from Me? How can your concern not be in what I possess when you inevitably return to Me? (continued...)

Inevitably, O Musa! Make Me your fortress, and deposit with Me your treasure of righteous deeds, and fear Me and fear none other than Me — to Me is the return. O Musa, have mercy on one who is below you in creation, and do not envy one who is above you, for envy consumes good deeds as fire consumes firewood. O Musa, the two sons of Adam humbled themselves in their station hoping to attain My favor and mercy, so they offered a sacrifice, and I do not accept except from the God-fearing — and what came of their affair you already know. So how can you trust a companion after a brother and a minister? O Musa, put down arrogance, abandon pride, and remember that you are a dweller of the grave — let that prevent you from desires. O Musa, hasten repentance, delay sin, and be patient in lingering before Me in prayer, and hope in none other than Me — take Me as a shield against hardships and a fortress against calamities. O Musa, how can a creature humble itself before Me when it does not know My favor upon it? And how can it know My favor upon it when it does not look into it? And how can it look into it when

...and it does not hope for a reward, and how can it hope for a reward when it has contented itself with this world and taken it as a home and leaned upon it with the leaning of the wrongdoers? O Musa, compete in good with those who are worthy of it, for good is as its name; and leave evil for every person who is infatuated with it. O Musa, make your tongue behind your heart so that you may be safe, and increase My remembrance by night and day so that you may profit, and do not follow errors so that you may regret — for errors lead to the Fire. O Musa, speak well to those who abandon sins, be their companion and take them as brothers in your private life, and strive alongside them and they will strive alongside you. O Musa, death will come to you inevitably, so provision yourself with the provision of one who journeys to his certain destination — arriving with certainty. O Musa, whatever is intended for My sake, even if little, is much; and whatever is intended for other than Me, even if much, is little. And the best of your days is the one that lies before you — so see what day it is, and prepare its answer, for you will be made to stand and be questioned. Take your admonition from time and its people, for the long time is short and the short is long, and everything is passing — so act as though you see the reward of your action so that it becomes most enticing for you in the Hereafter. Inevitably: what remains of the world is like what has already passed of it, and every worker works with insight and example, so seek provision for yourself, O son of Imran — perhaps you will succeed tomorrow on the day of questioning. For therein

For therein the falsifiers will lose. O Musa, cast your two palms down in humility before Me, as the action of a slave crying out to his master — for if you do that, you will be shown mercy, and I am the most Noble of the powerful. O Musa, ask Me from My favor and mercy, for they are both in My hand — no one possesses them but Me. And look, when you ask Me, what is your eagerness for what is with Me — for every worker there is a recompense, and the ingrate may be requited for what they strove for. O Musa, be at ease from the world, and turn away from it, for it is not yours and you are not for it. What do you have to do with the abode of the wrongdoers except for the one who works good in it — for it is for him an excellent abode! O Musa, whatever I command you, hear it and do whatever I show you. Take the realities of the Torah to your chest and be wakeful with it in the hours of the night and day, and do not allow the children of this world into your chest — lest they make it a nest like the nest of a bird. O Musa, the children of this world and its people are trials for one another — everyone adorned with what they are in — and the true believer is one for whom the Hereafter is adorned: he gazes upon it without tiring. Its desire has interposed between him and the pleasure of this life — driving him at dawn like a rider pressing toward his goal. He spends his day in grief and ends his evening in sorrow. How blessed is he, if only the veil were lifted — what would he behold of joy!

What would he behold of joy! O Musa, the world is just a drop — neither a reward for the believer nor a punishment for the wicked. So long is the woe for one who sold the recompense of his return for a morsel that did not remain and a taste that did not last. And so be as I have commanded you, for all My command is right guidance. O Musa, when you see wealth coming, say: a sin whose punishment has been hastened for me. And when you see poverty coming, say: welcome, O emblem of the righteous! And do not be a tyrant and wrongdoer, and do not be a companion of the wrongdoers. O Musa, no matter how long a lifespan, its end is blameworthy; and what harm is it to you what has been withheld from you when its final outcome is praised? O Musa, the Book has cried out to you with a cry about what you are heading toward — so how can the eyes sleep upon this? Or how can a people find the pleasure of life, were it not for the persistence in heedlessness, the following of wretchedness, the succession of desire? And beyond this

And beyond this, the truthful ones grieve. O Musa, command My servants to call upon Me for whatever may befall them, after they affirm for Me that I am the most Merciful of the merciful, the Answerer of the distressed; and I remove affliction and I change times and I bring ease and I appreciate the small and I reward the abundant and I enrich the poor — and I am the Ever-Lasting, the Mighty, the Powerful. So whoever takes refuge with you and comes to you from among the sinners, say: welcome and at ease, O spacious expanse of the expanse of the Lord of the Worlds! And seek forgiveness for them and be for them as one of them, and do not extend over them by reason of what I have given you of My favor. And tell them to ask of Me from My favor and mercy, for no one possesses it except Me — and I am the Possessor of the immense bounty. How blessed are you, O Musa, shelter of the sinners, companion of the distressed, seeker of forgiveness for the guilty — you are with Me in the station of the approved! So call on Me with a pure heart and a truthful tongue, and be as I have commanded you. Obey My command and do not extend over My servants with what does not originate from you. And draw near to Me — for I am near to you. For truly, I have not asked you what would burden you with its weight and its carrying. I have only asked you to call upon Me so that I respond to you, and to ask Me so that I give you, and to draw near to Me by what you have received from Me in its interpretation — and upon Me is the completion of its sending down.

...what you have received from Me in its interpretation — and upon Me is the completion of its sending down. O Musa, look at the earth — for soon it will be your grave. And raise your eyes to the sky, for above you in it is a Great Sovereign. And weep over yourself as long as you remain in this world, and fear destruction and perils, and let not the adornment and flowering of this world deceive you, and do not be content with injustice and do not be an oppressor — for I am watching the oppressor until I give the oppressed victory over him. O Musa, a good deed is tenfold in recompense, and from a single evil comes ruin. Do not associate partners with Me — it is not permissible for you to associate partners with Me. Be near and upright, and supplicate with the supplication of the one who yearns and desires what is with Me, repentant over what his hands have sent forward — for the darkness of the night is erased by the day, and likewise evil is erased by good. And the darkness of night comes upon the light of day, and likewise evil comes upon the glorious good deed and darkens it.

ai.seo_question: What did Allah say to Prophet Musa in the hadith of munajaat from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This is one of the most comprehensive divine discourses (munajaat) narrated in Shia hadith literature. Transmitted through a mursal (raised) chain, it presents an extended conversation in which Allah addresses Prophet Musa (AS) with a sweeping set of moral, spiritual, and theological teachings. Contextually, munajaat literature was a recognized genre of intimate divine-prophetic communication, and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (or the earlier Imam whose teaching this traces back to) preserved this as a model of Allah's direct guidance to His prophets. The discourse covers: the dangers of worldly attachment and long hope; the value of worn clothes and renewed hearts; the commandment to serve as Imam in prayer and judgment; a remarkable prophecy about Prophet Isa (AS) and the coming of Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) — including his descriptions, name (Ahmad/Muhammad), community, and the revelation of the Quran; obligations of prayer, zakat, and maintaining family ties; the treatment of beggars and the poor; divine omniscience and omnipotence; warnings against envy and arrogance; the inevitability of death and the Day of Judgment; and the invitation to sinners to seek forgiveness. The original audience — Shia Muslims transmitting this through their Imams — would have understood the prophecy about the Prophet of the red camel as a clear reference to Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), interpreting the descriptions as confirming his divine mandate across all scriptures.
